Folks — I exported the HubSpot attribution table and included it as hubspot-attribution-export.csv (attached to this thread). Notes on methodology I used:

1) First-touch: source that generated the contact (if contact created because of event form, first-touch = event).
2) First-engagement: earliest marketing interaction (email open/click, webinar attendance); if pre-existing outreach happened (SDR activity logged before event attendance), we mark event as "influenced" but not first-touch.
3) Multi-touch weighting: for the summary sheet I applied a simple 50/30/20 split across first-touch / opportunity-create / last-touch. That produced the numbers Ava shared.

Specific to Ben's calls:
- DW-4482: contact was created 2026-01-12 from an SDR outbound sequence, opportunity created 2026-02-02. Webinar attendance 2026-02-19. Under first-touch rules it is NOT event-sourced. It shows up as influenced (30% weight in our sheet).
- DW-4479: similar pattern; contact already in HS with active task history.

I can re-run a stricter rule set (event gets credit only if contact created within +/- 2 days of event date and no prior sequence activity) and regenerate the summary. That should reduce influenced ACV by ~28%.

—Marcus Lin
Revenue Operations Analyst

Subject: Re: Q1 Developer Webinar — Postmortem & Pipeline Credit (Postmortem notes + next steps)

Thanks all — based on Marcus's calc and Ben's examples I put together a short retro and proposed changes to attribution to reduce these disputes going forward. Summary below (full doc in Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c_webinar_postmortem):

Retro highlights:
- What went well: strong partner co-marketing (CloudScale), high attendance (1.5K registrants, 420 live attendees), good session NPS.
- What hurt clarity: our current "influenced" label is used inconsistently by RevOps and Marketing; sales reads it as "sourced."

Proposed immediate changes (apply for all webinars going forward):
1) Change rollup labels: use "Event-sourced" only when contact create date is within +/-2 days of event and no prior sequence tasks exist.
2) Maintain "Event-influenced" for multi-touch credit but report it separately on the marketing dashboard (no changes to SFDC lead source fields).
3) RevOps to publish a reconciliation CSV (fields Ben requested) within 48 hours of a major event.
4) Marketing to include an "attendee origin" column in the master list (form / partner / direct invite / existing-contact) so matching is explicit.

Action items:
- Marcus: rerun the summary with the stricter rule and send updated numbers by EOD Thu (2026-03-04).
- Ben: provide final list of contested deals (if any) by EOD Wed (2026-03-03).
- Laura: note label changes and include "Net new sourced pipeline" metric in the Q1 dashboard.

Thanks — I think this will close the loop and prevent inflation in future rollups.

—Ava
